title: ANTShapes Benchmarking Datasets for Event-Based Neuromorphic Object Classification
abstract: arXiv:2608.27150v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Object classification in event-based computer vision is a task that is attracting considerable research attention. Event-based object classification is a fundamental task in the fields of security and applied computer vision, which typically use synchronous frame-based cameras and computing pipelines for operation. This approach has several practical flaws. The size, weight and power consumption of the device could prohibit deployment at the extreme edge or in covert sensing environments. Besides this, there are security concerns inherent in cloud-based or other off-device computation approaches due to the requirement of sending and receiving potentially sensitive data. Furthermore, this transmission of data introduces latency and requires consistent connectivity to the cloud infrastructure to function.   The use of Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) hosted on neuromorphic devices attempts to solve several issues present in this convention

translated_title: ANTShapes：用于事件驱动神经形态物体分类的基准数据集
translated_abstract: 事件驱动计算机视觉中的物体分类是一项吸引大量研究关注的任务。事件驱动的物体分类是安全与应用计算机视觉领域的一项基础任务，通常依赖同步帧式相机和计算流水线进行操作。这种方法存在若干实际缺陷。设备的尺寸、重量和功耗可能阻碍其在极端边缘或隐蔽传感环境中的部署。此外，基于云或其他设备外计算方法存在固有的安全顾虑，因为需要发送和接收潜在敏感数据。而且，这种数据传输会引入延迟，并要求持续连接到云基础设施才能运行。使用托管在神经形态设备上的脉冲神经网络（SNN）试图解决这一传统方法中存在的几个问题。
tldr: 本文提出了ANTShapes基准数据集，用于事件驱动神经形态物体分类，旨在解决传统帧式相机在边缘部署、功耗、安全性和延迟方面的缺陷。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the ANTShapes benchmark datasets for event-based neuromorphic object classification, addressing flaws in conventional frame-based methods regarding edge deployment, power, security, and latency.
